samples.text: Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, the adoption of this resolution is not the end of our journey. The adoption of this resolution is now the beginning of our resolution. For us, As African, the adoption of this resolution is far more than a cartographic decision. The adoption of this resolution is an act of recognition. The adoption of this resolution is an act of reparation. The adoption of this resolution, it's an act of justice. The adoption of this resolution is for justice in the world. That way, today, we have not redrawn the world. We have corrected the way in which the world is represented. Togo intends to build on this historic momentum. We count on the continued mobilization of Member States of the United Nations and its agencies, of regional organizations, of scientific institutions and of technology platforms to translate this resolution into concrete action. Because a resolution must not remain a text. Resolution must become action. Action must become knowledge. Knowledge must become education. And education must become understanding among peoples. As we say, a fairer map does not redraw the border of the world. It transforms the way we see the world ourself. Togo now wishes to move from resolution to action. We propose the opening of a new phase of international cooperation, bringing together the member state, the agency of United Nation, we say scientific and academic institution, geographer and cartographers, historian, educators, young people, and the innovators shaping the technologies of tomorrow, including artificial intelligence. Our objective is clear, dear friends, to make cartography an even more powerful instrument of knowledge, education, inclusion, and mutual understanding amongst people. We must encourage research We must develop also a new education tools for our generation. Excellencies, the digital revolution give us the issue and in turn a new dimension. Billion of people now consult maps every day on their phones, their computers and digital platform. Children, for example, discover the world through the digital maps. The businessmen make decision using cartographic data.

The government also rely on special information and artificial intelligence system increasingly interpret our planet through digital data and cartographic representation. The question before us. Therefore, it's no longer only about printed maps. It's about the digital image of our planet that we are transmitting to the generation of tomorrow. Ladies and gentlemen, we also want Correct the Map to become a dialogue between generations. We want young people to have the opportunity to look at our planet with a fresh eyes. We want schools, universities, and research institution to become places where the representation of our world can be studied, questioned, and understood. We want African cartographers to contribute We want European cartographers to contribute. We want Asian cartographers to contribute. We want cartographers from America, from Arab region, Pacific, and every region in the world to contribute, because the world belongs to all of us. And because the way we represent our world should be a conversation open to all. Excellencies, today, Togo launches an appeal, an appeal to all member states, an appeal to international organizations, an appeal to the scientific community, an appeal to educators, an appeal to innovators, an appeal to the young people of the world. Let us correct the map an international laboratory for reflection, refresh, and innovation on the representation of our world. Let us transform this resolution into a program of cooperation. Let us transform an idea into knowledge. Let us transform knowledge into education, and let us transform education into greater understanding among the people we serve. We know now what we have to do for our generation. We are not here simply to correct a map. We are here to help correct a way of seeing, a way of seeing some things inherited from the past, a way of seeing that can be enriched by science, A way of seeing that can be rebalanced by our knowledge. And ultimately, a way of seeing that reminds us of one simple truth. We share our planet. We share our humanity.
